analysis:
Examined all supplied fixture text, patches and file metadata. libs/darkbloom-cluster/Tests/PlacementChecks/Golden/layouts/gemma-4-26b-qat-4bit.json:1 adds tensor_parallel_v1, routed-expert accounting and a two-rank heads/expert-channel layout with float32 sealed-all-gather reductions. Artifact/configuration hashes, token bounds, existing layer costs and per-rank request charges remain unchanged. Divided plus replicated layer/ingress/egress bytes match the existing loaded-byte totals. gemma-4-26b-8bit.json:1 contains corresponding head fields; its supplied BASE patch is truncated. gemma-4-26b.json has metadata and a truncated BASE-only patch excerpt, limiting comparison.
No concrete security regression is established by these test expectations alone. They neither implement authorization/encryption nor prove live policy or correct inference. No cache scope, disk metadata, TTL or KEK behavior under T-041 is changed in the supplied evidence. There is no visible change to credentials, privileged helpers, installers or billing.
Integration should reconcile these expectations with the changed layout generator, placement admission and execution paths: verify conservative expert/transient/KV accounting and request bounds (A-018/TB-007), authenticated and request-bound reduction traffic protecting A-001 (TB-002/T-008), and authorization/revocation for every participating adversarial provider (TB-011/T-053). The sealed_all_gather_sum_v1 label is not evidence that those controls are enforced. Any new live multi-provider boundary should be checked against the canonical model; these fixtures do not establish its activation. Missing runtime source and the incomplete gemma-4-26b.json comparison remain coverage limits for integration, not findings.
